sentences.text: Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is repeat second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant,
in connection with FIR/Crime No.343/2023, Date:-
(Not mentioned) registered at P.S.-Alot, District- Ratlam (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 366, 344, 376(2) (N) of the IPC.
2.
First bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 23.011.2023.
3. Prosecution story in brief is that, on 02.06.2023 applicant took the prosecutrix to many places and kept her with him till 13.06.2023.
Meanwhile he committed rape upon her several times.

On Kailash @ Keliya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93965657/
1 13.06.2023 prosecutrix was recovered from the possession of the applicant.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that prosecutrix is major lady and she voluntarily went with the applicant.
She was also consenting party for sexual intercourse.

It is further submitted that after dismissal of first bail application of the applicant prosecutrix (P.W.-1) and her uncle (Mausa) (P.W.-2) have been examined before the trial Court but they are turned hostile and have not supported the case of the prosecution.
Applicant is in custody since 14.06.2023.
Conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time for its disposal.
Under these circumstances, prayer is made for grant of bail to the applicant.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer of the applicant and prays for rejection of the application.

6. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also considering the facts and circumstances, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Hence, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant- KAILASH @ KELIYA be released on bail upon his/her furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his/her appearance before the trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.
It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

8. M.Cr.C. stands disposed of, accordingly.
C.c.
as per rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE ajit Kailash @ Keliya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93965657/
